extracted.intended_audience: prospective students, performers, fans, and researchers interested in The Groundlings' history and training practices
extracted.subtask_description: A historical/organizational overview of The Groundlings theatre and school describing how performers were selected, trained, and how shows and creative decisions were produced. Useful for understanding the company's training pipeline, show formats, and artistic philosophy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership eligibility (early fee and later auditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: “membership at that time required only that you pay $25 to attend workshops” ... later: “Auditions became required to join.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originally membership required a $25 workshop fee; as the company grew, formal auditions were instituted. Membership size grew (to ~90 performers at one point) and later structures included caps (Main Company now capped at 30 members).

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop material in workshops and perform best work
rubrics_metrics.description: “would develop material in the workshops and then perform the best work in the weekend shows.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshops were the primary development space; material created in workshops was curated so that the strongest pieces were presented in public revues and weekend shows. The text notes extensive workshop activity (eventually 'seven days a week') supporting continuous development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progression through curriculum and voting for company membership
rubrics_metrics.description: “After ascending through the curriculum and honing their improv and writing skills, the cream of the crop were voted on by The Groundlings to decide if they were to join The Sunday Company. After further demonstration of their abilities in the weekly Sunday Show, the members were voted on once again in the hopes of becoming a Groundling.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection to higher company tiers is a multi-stage process: complete the curriculum, demonstrate abilities in performance (weekly shows), then be approved by peer voting. Demonstrated performance and peer evaluation are explicit gates to advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main Company collective artistic direction and democratic decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Main Company (now capped at 30 members) collectively acted as the organization's artistic director, democratically making business and creative decisions as a group. This remains true to this day.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artistic and some business decisions are made collectively by Main Company members rather than a single artistic director; democratic processes govern creative leadership and organizational choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and preserve a distinct improv/character/sketch comedy style
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Groundlings Revue (now commonly referred to as the Main Show) was the first show performed by the Main Company as they established the Groundlings improv, character, and sketch comedy style.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Productions are intended to reflect and refine an identifiable Groundlings style emphasizing improv, character work, and sketch comedy. Revues and shows serve to codify and display that style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular production schedule and multiple show formats
rubrics_metrics.description: “Initially, there would be one or two Revues a year. By the 1990's, three shows a year was the norm. And in 2007, the company decided to do four shows per year, in addition to a special holiday show in December.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization maintains a steady cadence of revues and also programs alternative format shows (examples from 1981 onward include 'The Pee-Wee Herman Show', 'Cooking With Gas', long-form improv like the 'Crazy Uncle Joe Show', and many one-off formats). Consistent output and format variety are part of the institution's practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: School curriculum, scale, and role as a training ground
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Groundlings School officially began in 1979 ... After ascending through the curriculum ...” and later: “With over 8000 improv and sketch comedy students per year, The Groundlings has become the pre-eminent training ground for comedy in Los Angeles and beyond.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The school offers a progressive curriculum intended to develop improv and writing skills; large annual enrollment and a multi-level pipeline (classes → Sunday Company → Main Company) position the school as a central training institution. Advancement through the curriculum is a prerequisite for company consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incubation of characters and sketches for broader media success
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: Paul Reubens' Pee-Wee Herman developed in Groundlings workshops and Revues and went on to HBO special, films, TV; many Main Show scenes/characters were turned into TV favorites; the site lists numerous alumni who moved to SNL, Mad TV, films, and YouTube successes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producing characters and sketches intended for transfer to television, film, and digital media is an implicit goal. The historical record is cited as evidence that characters developed on stage can and have been adapted into larger media platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder's teaching philosophy: 'no mistakes' and commitment to the work
rubrics_metrics.description: “He believed there were no mistakes and all forms of creativity were worthy of exploration. ... Gary believed in a deep commitment to one’s craft. ... He was compelled to inspire artists to find their truest selves through 'the work.'”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaching emphasizes experimentation, authenticity, and persistent practice. The pedagogical stance encourages risk-taking, reframing errors as material, and sustained dedication to craft rather than perfectionism.
